2203.describe_en: High-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows a single blast with a round nucleus occupying most of the cell, finely dispersed chromatin, faint nucleoli, and a thin rim of deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm. Small cytoplasmic projections or blebs are present at the cell surface (arrow). No granules or Auer rods are seen. The morphology is that of a lymphoblast; cytoplasmic blebs are nonspecific and do not indicate lineage or genotype. Findings are consistent with acute lymphoblastic leukemia, with Philadelphia chromosome status requiring cytogenetic or molecular confirmation.

ddx.vs: Megakaryoblasts characteristically show prominent cytoplasmic blebbing too, but express CD41/CD61 and lack TdT and B-lymphoid markers.
Hairy cells have mature oval nuclei and abundant pale gray-blue cytoplasm with circumferential fine projections, not blastic chromatin with scant cytoplasm.
Myeloblasts tend to have more cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, and may contain azurophilic granules or Auer rods with MPO positivity.

2139.recognize_zh: 視野中可見多個核圓、染色質細緻、胞質深藍的芽細胞，旁邊有核分葉異常且顆粒稀少的顆粒球系細胞與核形不規則的紅血球前驅細胞；但單一視野中多系發育不良的程度有限，需結合全片計數判讀。
features: Several blasts with round nuclei, fine chromatin, and deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Hypogranular myeloid cell with abnormal nuclear lobation (upper center)
Erythroid precursors with irregular nuclear contours and nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony
Scattered small lymphocytes and orthochromatic normoblasts
Poikilocytic red cells in background
2139.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows several blasts with round nuclei, fine chromatin, and moderate deeply basophilic cytoplasm, admixed with a hypogranular myeloid cell with abnormal nuclear lobation and erythroid precursors showing irregular nuclear contours. Small lymphocytes and late normoblasts are also present. The degree of multilineage dysplasia cannot be quantified from this single field. Findings are suggestive of acute myeloid leukemia with dysplastic features, compatible with AML with myelodysplasia-related changes when blast count and lineage dysplasia criteria are met.

ddx.vs: Separated by blast percentage (<20% in MDS), which requires a 500-cell differential rather than a single field.
These lack ≥50% dysplasia in two or more lineages and MDS-defining cytogenetic abnormalities.
Megaloblastic change shows nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony and giant metamyelocytes but no increase in blasts, and corrects with B12/folate.

1883.recognize_zh: 脾臟切片中紅髓被單一形態、間距均勻的小型細胞浸潤，細胞核呈圓形至腎形、細胞質淡而清，並形成充滿紅血球的血湖（red blood cell lakes / pseudosinuses），符合毛狀細胞白血病的脾臟紅髓型態。
features: Diffuse red pulp infiltrate of monotonous small to medium cells
Round, oval to bean-shaped (reniform) nuclei with bland chromatin
Moderate pale to clear cytoplasm giving evenly spaced 'fried-egg' spacing
Blood lakes (pseudosinuses) filled with red cells lined by tumor cells
No white pulp nodules or mitotic activity evident in this field
1883.describe_en: Section of spleen shows diffuse expansion of the red pulp by a monotonous population of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with oval to reniform nuclei, bland chromatin and moderate pale cytoplasm. Cells are evenly spaced, and there are prominent red cell lakes (pseudosinuses) lined by the neoplastic cells. White pulp is not identified in this field. Findings are consistent with splenic involvement by hairy cell leukemia; confirmation with annexin A1, CD103, CD25, TRAP and BRAF V600E is recommended.

ddx.vs: SMZL predominantly involves and expands the white pulp with biphasic nodules, whereas HCL is red-pulp-based with blood lakes and is annexin A1/BRAF V600E positive.

ddx.dx: Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma / HCL variant
ddx.vs: These also involve red pulp but lack annexin A1, CD25 and BRAF V600E, and HCL-v cells have prominent nucleoli.
HSTCL infiltrates sinusoids (not cords with blood lakes) with medium-sized T cells that are CD3+ and usually TCR gamma-delta, lacking B-cell markers.

1819.recognize_zh: 中央三顆巨大組織球的細胞質呈淡藍灰色、帶明顯纖維狀條紋（皺褶薄紙樣），各有一個小而偏位的核，與周圍的紅血球系及顆粒球前驅細胞相比體積大好幾倍，為典型高雪氏細胞（Gaucher cells）。
features: Cluster of very large histiocytes, several times the size of adjacent precursors
Abundant pale blue-grey cytoplasm with fibrillary 'wrinkled tissue paper' striations
Single small eccentric nucleus per cell with condensed chromatin
Surrounding normal erythroid and granulocytic precursors
Background erythrocytes; no cytoplasmic vacuoles or crystals
1819.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at high power shows a cluster of very large histiocytes with small eccentric nuclei and abundant pale blue-grey cytoplasm bearing fibrillary, wrinkled tissue paper-like striations. They are surrounded by normal-appearing erythroid and granulocytic precursors. No vacuolated foam cells or organisms are identified. Findings are consistent with Gaucher cells, supporting Gaucher disease pending glucocerebrosidase enzyme and GBA1 testing.

ddx.vs: Identical appearance but associated with high cell turnover disorders (CML, myeloma, thalassemia) and normal enzyme activity.
Foam cells have uniform small lipid vacuoles giving a bubbly cytoplasm.
Contain discrete blue-green ceroid granules rather than fibrillary cytoplasm.
Have large lobulated nuclei and granular pink cytoplasm rather than a small eccentric nucleus with striated cytoplasm.

1755.recognize_zh: 免疫染色（抗體未標示）中，少數散在的大型細胞呈棕色膜狀與核旁點狀（Golgi）陽性，中央細胞含兩個對稱的核（雙核Reed-Sternberg細胞樣），背景小淋巴球陰性，符合何杰金氏淋巴瘤中CD30或CD15陽性的HRS細胞。
features: Scattered large cells with strong brown membranous and paranuclear (Golgi-pattern) staining
Central binucleate cell with two mirror-image nuclei outlined by the stain, resembling a Reed-Sternberg cell
Mononuclear Hodgkin cells with ring-like membrane staining
Background of numerous small lymphocytes with unstained nuclei
Antibody is not labeled; the pattern fits CD30 or CD15
1755.describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain shows scattered large cells with strong membranous and paranuclear dot-like staining, including a central binucleate Reed-Sternberg-like cell and several mononuclear Hodgkin cells, set in a background of negative small lymphocytes. The antibody is not specified in the image, but the membrane-plus-Golgi pattern is typical of CD30 or CD15 in Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells. Findings are consistent with classic Hodgkin lymphoma; a full panel including CD15, CD30, PAX5, CD20, CD45, and EBER is recommended.

ddx.vs: ALCL cells form sheets or sinus-filling aggregates, are CD15 usually negative, PAX5 negative, and often ALK positive rather than scattered HRS cells.
LP cells are CD30 and CD15 negative and strongly CD20 positive within nodules of small B cells.
The scattered large cells are CD20 and BCL6 positive and CD30/CD15 negative in a background of T cells and histiocytes.
Reactive immunoblasts are CD15 negative, strongly CD20/PAX5 positive, and occur in a polymorphous expanded paracortex.

1627.recognize_zh: 右上角為淋巴結周圍脂肪與纖維被膜，其下為被膜下竇與皮質；皮質由密集小淋巴球構成，間有較淡、帶較多細胞質的細胞形成斑駁區，未見結構破壞，是正常淋巴結邊緣的低倍樣貌。
features: Perinodal adipose tissue and fibrous capsule at the upper right
Subcapsular sinus beneath the capsule containing scattered pale cells
Cortex composed of densely packed small round lymphocytes
Irregular paler zones with larger cells and more cytoplasm imparting a mottled pattern
No well-formed germinal center in this field; no capsular infiltration by lymphocytes
1627.describe_en: Section of lymph node at low-to-medium power shows perinodal fat, an intact fibrous capsule and an underlying subcapsular sinus. The cortex consists of densely packed small lymphocytes with interspersed paler zones containing larger cells with more abundant cytoplasm, producing a mottled appearance. No germinal center is included in this field, and there is no extracapsular extension or monotonous atypical infiltrate. Findings are consistent with normal lymph node cortex.

ddx.vs: SLL diffusely effaces the node with pale proliferation centers and obliterates sinuses, whereas here the capsule and subcapsular sinus are intact.
MCL shows a monotonous population of slightly irregular small cells with hyalinized vessels and cyclin D1 positivity, without the mixed mottled pattern seen here.

1435.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片兩格：箭頭所指的顆粒球系細胞（含雙核、C 形核的帶狀核及較大前驅細胞）細胞質淡粉、幾乎沒有顆粒，與旁邊顆粒粗大的正常早幼粒細胞對比明顯，代表顆粒球發育異常（hypogranulation）。
features: Myeloid cells (arrows) with abundant pale, agranular or markedly hypogranular cytoplasm
Left panel: arrowed cells include a binucleated/bilobed granulocytic precursor with pale cytoplasm
Right panel: agranular band-like cell with a C-shaped nucleus, and a large precursor with pale hypogranular cytoplasm (double arrows)
Internal control: a promyelocyte with normal coarse azurophilic granules for comparison (left panel, center)
Background erythroid precursors with dense nuclei and mixed maturing myeloid cells
1435.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (two fields) shows granulocytic precursors with abundant pale, agranular to markedly hypogranular cytoplasm (arrows), including a binucleated precursor and an agranular band form with a C-shaped nucleus, in contrast to an adjacent promyelocyte with normal coarse azurophilic granules. Erythroid precursors and maturing myeloid elements are present in the background. Hypogranulation of neutrophil lineage cells is a recognized feature of dysgranulopoiesis; the findings support a myelodysplastic syndrome, consistent with the stated diagnosis of MDS with multilineage dysplasia when dysplasia is present in >=10% of cells of two or more lineages.

ddx.dx: Smear or staining artifact (poor granule staining)
ddx.vs: Artifact affects all cells uniformly, whereas here adjacent promyelocytes retain well-stained coarse granules.
Microgranular APL shows sheets of bilobed abnormal promyelocytes with dust-like granules and PML-RARA, not scattered dysplastic maturing cells.

ddx.dx: Drug or toxin effect (e.g., G-CSF, chemotherapy, mycophenolate)
ddx.vs: Drug-related dysgranulopoiesis is transient and lacks clonal cytogenetic or molecular abnormalities; clinical history is essential.

ddx.dx: Acquired or congenital neutrophil granule defects
ddx.vs: Isolated granule deficiency affects only mature neutrophils without dysplasia in other lineages.

60507.recognize_zh: 大細胞的核偏心、圓至卵圓且一側略扁平，染色質比前骨髓細胞更聚集、看不到核仁，細胞質豐富並帶細小淡紫粉紅顆粒，屬骨髓細胞（myelocyte）。
features: Large cell, about twice the diameter of adjacent red cells
Eccentric, oval nucleus with a flattened edge and no indentation
Moderately condensed chromatin without visible nucleoli
Abundant cytoplasm with a bluish tint containing fine lilac-pink specific granules and scattered pale granular areas
No paranuclear hof prominence, Auer rods or coarse azurophilic granule clusters
60507.describe_en: High-power smear shows a large granulocytic precursor with an eccentric oval nucleus, moderately condensed chromatin and no visible nucleoli. The cytoplasm is abundant, faintly basophilic and contains numerous fine lilac-pink secondary granules. No nuclear indentation, Auer rods or dysplastic features are present. Findings are consistent with a myelocyte; its presence in peripheral blood indicates a left shift, as seen in infection, growth factor effect, marrow infiltration or myeloid neoplasms.

ddx.vs: Promyelocytes have finer chromatin, often a visible nucleolus, a prominent Golgi hof and coarse purple azurophilic granules rather than fine lilac specific granules.
Metamyelocytes have a kidney-shaped nucleus with an indentation less than half the nuclear width and more condensed chromatin.
Monocytes have folded nuclei with lacy chromatin and grey-blue vacuolated cytoplasm with dust-like granules rather than pink specific granules.

91.recognize_zh: 皮膚真皮內有密集、結節狀圍繞毛囊的小至中型淋巴球浸潤，表皮沒有明顯親表皮性（epidermotropism），CD3 陽性 T 細胞為主並混有不少 CD20 陽性小 B 細胞，另見零星較大的陽性細胞，符合原發性皮膚 CD4 陽性小/中型 T 細胞淋巴增生性疾患。
features: Dense nodular to diffuse dermal lymphoid infiltrate surrounding hair follicles, with a narrow uninvolved band beneath the epidermis
No significant epidermotropism; the overlying epidermis and adnexal epithelium are largely spared
Predominantly small to medium lymphocytes with round to slightly irregular nuclei and dense chromatin
Scattered larger cells with vesicular nuclei and small nucleoli admixed with histiocytes
IHC: sheets of CD3-type membranous T-cell staining with a substantial admixed B-cell population and a minor subset positive for a second T-cell marker
Only rare large cells positive on one stain (isolated membranous-staining large cell), without sheets of large atypical cells
91.describe_en: Skin biopsy shows a dense nodular to diffuse lymphoid infiltrate occupying the dermis and surrounding hair follicles, with relative sparing of the epidermis and no significant epidermotropism. The infiltrate is composed predominantly of small to medium-sized lymphocytes with slightly irregular nuclei, admixed with scattered larger cells with vesicular chromatin, histiocytes, and occasional plasma cells; sheets of large atypical cells are not seen. Immunohistochemistry shows a T-cell-predominant infiltrate with strong membranous staining, a substantial admixed population of reactive B cells, a smaller subset reactive for a second T-cell marker, and only rare large positive cells on another stain (individual marker labels are not provided in the images). Findings are consistent with primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder, in the appropriate clinical setting of a solitary nodule.

ddx.vs: MF has a history of patches/plaques and epidermotropic atypical cerebriform cells, whereas this lesion is a solitary nodule with a dermal infiltrate and a spared epidermis.
PCMZL is dominated by CD20+ marginal zone B cells and light-chain-restricted plasma cells, whereas here CD3+ T cells predominate and B cells are a reactive admixture.
Morphology overlaps heavily; PCSMLPD shows a dominant CD4+ small/medium T-cell population with PD-1+ larger cells and frequently a clonal TCR rearrangement, so ancillary studies are needed.

ddx.dx: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS involving skin
ddx.vs: PTCL shows sheets of large pleomorphic T cells, often with antigen loss, high proliferation and systemic disease, unlike the predominantly small/medium cells with few large cells seen here.

91.stain: H&E; IHC (T- and B-cell markers, not labeled)
captions: H&E, low power: dense dermal and perifollicular lymphoid infiltrate beneath intact epidermis
H&E, medium power: infiltrate around a follicle without epidermotropism
H&E, high power: small to medium lymphocytes with scattered larger vesicular cells and histiocytes
IHC, low power (marker not labeled): nodular aggregates of positive lymphocytes in the dermis
Membranous T-cell-type IHC: dense positive infiltrate sparing adnexal epithelium
Membranous T-cell-type IHC: positive infiltrate below epidermis with few intraepidermal cells
IHC (marker not labeled): scattered positive lymphocytes, a minor subset
IHC (marker not labeled): numerous positive cells forming a large component of the infiltrate
IHC (marker not labeled): scattered positive small cells
IHC, high power (marker not labeled): a single large positive cell among negative small lymphocytes
IHC (marker not labeled): diffuse cytoplasmic/membranous staining of the infiltrate

27.recognize_zh: 血液與骨髓抹片可見芽細胞增加，合併多系發育不良：顆粒稀少的嗜中性球、假 Pelger 核、紅血球前驅細胞核分葉/出芽、切片中核葉分離的異常巨核細胞；骨髓切片富細胞，流式顯示 CD34+/CD117+/CD13+ 骨髓性芽細胞，符合 MDS 伴隨芽細胞增加（RAEB）。
features: Increased blasts in blood and marrow: medium-to-large cells with high N:C ratio, fine chromatin, visible nucleoli and scant to moderate agranular basophilic cytoplasm
Dysgranulopoiesis: hypogranular neutrophils and myeloid precursors with pale cytoplasm, hyposegmented (pseudo-Pelger-like) nuclei
Dyserythropoiesis: erythroid precursors with nuclear lobulation/budding and megaloblastoid chromatin
Dysmegakaryopoiesis on biopsy: megakaryocytes with multiple widely separated round nuclei and small hypolobated forms
Hypercellular marrow biopsy with reduced fat; IHC highlights increased scattered interstitial positive mononuclear cells (antigen not labeled, likely CD34)
Flow cytometry: CD45-dim, low-SSC blast gate that is CD34+, CD117+, CD13+, HLA-DR+, partial CD33 and partial aberrant CD56, CD19-, CD7-, CD14-
27.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows anisopoikilocytosis with ovalocytes and teardrop cells, hypogranular neutrophils and circulating blasts with fine chromatin, nucleoli and scant basophilic cytoplasm; platelets appear reduced at low power. The bone marrow aspirate shows increased blasts with multilineage dysplasia, including hypogranular and hyposegmented granulocytes and erythroid precursors with nuclear lobulation and megaloblastoid change. The core biopsy is hypercellular with dysplastic megakaryocytes, including forms with multiple separated nuclei, and immunohistochemistry (antigen not labeled) highlights increased interstitial positive mononuclear cells without large aggregates. Flow cytometry identifies a CD45-dim myeloid blast population expressing CD34, CD117, CD13 and HLA-DR with partial CD33 and aberrant partial CD56, and lacking CD19, CD7 and CD14. The blast percentage must be established by manual differential count; findings are consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome with excess blasts (RAEB).

ddx.vs: AML requires >=20% blasts in blood or marrow (or a defining genetic lesion), whereas MDS-EB has 5-19% marrow or 2-19% blood blasts on manual count.
Megaloblastic anemia shows hypersegmented neutrophils, giant metamyelocytes and nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony without increased CD34+ blasts, and corrects with vitamin replacement.

ddx.dx: Reactive/regenerating marrow after chemotherapy or G-CSF
ddx.vs: Regenerating marrow shows left-shifted but granulated myeloid precursors with synchronous maturation and a transient CD34+ increase without aberrant CD56 or persistent dysplasia.
CMML requires persistent peripheral monocytosis (>=0.5 x10^9/L and >=10% of WBC), which is not evident in these fields.

Bone marrow aspirate: hypogranular myeloid precursors and erythroid precursors

Bone marrow aspirate: two blasts with fine chromatin and nucleoli beside a hypogranular band
Bone marrow aspirate: blasts and immature myeloid cells with sparse granulation and abnormal nuclear shapes
Bone marrow biopsy, low power: hypercellular marrow with scattered megakaryocytes
Bone marrow biopsy: hypercellular marrow with immature cells and small megakaryocytes
Bone marrow biopsy, high power: dysplastic megakaryocyte with multiple widely separated round nuclei
IHC (antigen not labeled, likely CD34): increased scattered interstitial positive mononuclear cells
Flow cytometry: CD45-dim blasts CD34+ CD117+ CD13+ HLA-DR+ with partial CD33 and CD56, CD19- CD7- CD14-
Peripheral blood, high power: circulating blast with nucleoli and basophilic cytoplasm
